This happens when another app is the default handler of the contactless category.

Ten slots on one screen, each with three actions:

1. Copy - hold a card or tag against the back of the phone. The app stores everything the tag hands out: UID, technologies, ATQA and SAK, NDEF, every application that answers a SELECT over ISO-DEP, and the MIFARE memory that a known key unlocks.

2. Transmit - the phone answers an NFC reader as that card (host card emulation). Only one slot can be transmitted at a time, tap the button again to stop.

3. Delete - empties the slot.

Tap a slot to see its data, rename it or add an AID by hand.

WHAT THE PHONE CAN TRANSMIT
Android can only emulate ISO-DEP (ISO 14443-4) applications, that is cards a reader talks to with APDU commands. MIFARE Classic, MIFARE Ultralight, NTAG and other low level tags cannot be transmitted: the NFC controller does not expose those modes to apps. Their data is still copied and can be inspected.

The phone always presents its own UID. Android does not allow changing the UID in card emulation mode, so readers that verify the serial number will reject it.

Bank cards are not supported. Their keys live in a secure element and every transaction uses a one time cryptogram, so replaying copied answers cannot work.

Copy and transmit only cards that you own or are allowed to use.
